narrative: 一张桌子的边缘从1960年代的厨房一直延伸进当代的一家餐馆。一张脸被一分为二：左边是你想象中的那场聚会，右边是你真正得到的那场聚会。
一条线，两个世界。当一次分割应该感觉像一个统一的有机体，而不是两台电视机时使用它。
当两块画面没有共享的轮廓、只是同时存在时，这个手法就用错了——那只是普通的分屏（Split Screen）。当你从一个完整画面剪到另一个与之呼应的完整画面时，这个手法也用错了——那是匹配剪辑（Match Cut）或图形匹配（Graphic Match）。
这条分界线不是一道划痕，而是一条经过设计、眼睛可以顺着追踪下去的接缝。
how: 构图时让一条线、一条视线、一条地平线或一个运动矢量跨越这道边界延续下去。如果一个人的两个版本共享一张沙发，就要匹配好头部的比例。
除非“灯光也匹配”本身就是笑点，否则要让每个世界的布光各有其动机。提示词：match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space.
when: 用在双胞胎、双重人生、期望与现实的对比，或者一天中两个不同的时刻共存的道路上。如果两个空间在图形上不应该有接触，就不要用它。
如果你需要的只是一通电话，两个房间坦然地各自独立，那么一次干净的分割就足够了。
vs: 分屏是并列共存；匹配分割（Match Split）是一种形式上呼应或延续的分割方式。匹配剪辑则用一个完整的画面替换另一个完整的画面。
框中框是场景内部的一扇窗户。图形匹配发生在一次跨越时间的硬切之中，而不是一条同时存在的接缝上。
examples_film: 《天生一对》（The Parent Trap）把同一个女孩的两个版本安置在一个共享的图形之中，让这次分割本身成为一种关系。《和莎莫的500天》((500) Days of Summer)沿着一条清晰的接缝，把一场聚会分成期望和现实。
借用这条延续的线，而不是照搬情节本身。
mistakes: 最常见的误用近亲是一个通用的、视线不匹配的分屏，或者按顺序排列的匹配剪辑。破绽是：两段叠放的片段没有共享的线条，或者用了一次剪辑而不是一条同时存在的接缝。
解决办法是：设计好这条分界线，延续一个轮廓，同时保持两个世界并存。

faq.q: 电影中的“匹配分割”是什么？
faq.a: 匹配分割是一种被分割的画面，其中一条线、一次运动，或一个轮廓从一个世界延续进另一个世界。剪接点两侧同时可见，并在图形上互相关联。

faq.q: 匹配分割 vs 分屏
faq.a: 分屏同时展示两个场域。匹配分割是一种沿着接缝呼应或延续一条线的分割方式。所有的匹配分割都是分屏，但不是所有的分屏都能“匹配”。

faq.q: 什么时候该用匹配分割？
faq.a: 当一个轮廓应该同时属于两个世界时使用。不要把它用在一个没有共享几何关系的简单电话通话面板上。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写匹配分割的提示词？
faq.a: 点明延续的那条线以及两个半边画面。示例：Match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space. 要求两个画面同时存在，不要变形。

narrative: A table edge runs from a 1960s kitchen into a present-day diner. A face is halved: left is the party you imagined, right is the party you got.
One line, two worlds. Use it when a split should feel like one organism rather than two televisions.

It is the wrong tool when the panes have no shared contour and are only simultaneous: that is ordinary Split Screen. It is also the wrong tool when you cut from one full frame to another rhyming full frame: that is a Match Cut or Graphic Match.
The divide is not a scratch. It is a designed seam that the eye can follow.
how: Compose both halves so a line, eyeline, horizon, or motion vector continues across the boundary. Match scale of heads if two versions of one person share a couch.
Keep lighting motivated per world unless the gag is that light also matches. Prompt: match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space.
when: Use it for twins, double lives, expectation versus reality, a road that is two times of day. Do not use it if the two spaces should not touch graphically.
If you need a phone call with frankly separate rooms, a clean split is enough.
vs: Split Screen co-presents; match split is a split whose form rhymes or continues. A Match Cut replaces one full image with another.
Frame within Frame is a window in the set. Graphic Match happens across a hard cut in time, not across a simultaneous seam.
examples_film: The Parent Trap seats two versions of one girl in a shared graphic so the split is a relationship. (500) Days of Summer divides a party into expectation and reality along a readable seam.
Use the continued line, not the plot.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a generic Split Screen with unmatched eyelines, or a Match Cut in sequence. The tell: two stacked clips with no shared line, or a cut instead of a co-present seam.
The fix: design the divide, continue one contour, hold both worlds at once.

faq.q: What is Match Split in film?
faq.a: A match split is a divided frame where a line, motion, or contour continues from one world into the other. Both sides of the join are visible together and graphically related.
Split screen shows two fields at once. Match split is a split that rhymes or continues a line across the seam. All match splits are splits; not all splits match.

faq.q: When should I use Match Split?
faq.a: Use it when one contour should belong to two worlds at the same time. Do not use it for a simple phone-call panel with no shared geometry.

faq.q: How do I prompt Match Split for AI image or video?
faq.a: Name the continued line and both halves. Example: Match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space. Simultaneous panes, no morph.
